t.1.79.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yayāti, having been overtaken by old age and having returned to his own city, spoke these words to Yadu, his eldest and most excellent son.
t.1.79.2: Old age, wrinkles and grey hairs have overtaken me, my son, through the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, and yet I am not sated with youth.
t.1.79.3: O Yadu, take upon yourself my evil together with my old age; with your youth I would enjoy the objects of the senses.
t.1.79.5: With white beard and hair, wretched, slackened by old age, his limbs covered all over with wrinkles, unsightly, feeble and emaciated.
t.1.79.4: When a full thousand years have passed, I shall give your youth back to you and take upon myself once more my own evil, together with old age.
t.1.79.6: Unable to carry out his tasks, such a man is scorned by the young and by his own dependents as well; I do not desire that old age.
t.1.79.7: Since you, born of my own heart, do not give me your youth, therefore, my son, your offspring shall have no share in the kingdom.
t.1.79.9: But when a full thousand years have passed, I will give back your youth, and I will take upon myself again my own evil together with old age.
t.1.79.8: Turvasu, take upon yourself this affliction together with old age; with your youth, dear son, I would indeed enjoy the pleasures of the senses.
t.1.79.10: Turvasu said: I do not desire old age, father, which destroys the enjoyment of pleasures, which brings an end to strength and beauty, and which ruins intellect and vital breath.
t.1.79.11: Since you, born from my heart, do not give me your own youth, therefore, Turvasu, your progeny will go to utter extinction.
t.1.79.12: You fool, you shall be king over those whose customs and laws are confused, over those born of reversed caste unions, and over the meat-eating outcastes.
t.1.79.14: Having thus cursed Turvasu, his own son, Yayāti spoke these words to Druhyu, the son of Śarmiṣṭhā.
t.1.79.13: You shall hold sway among the wicked Mlecchas, who lust after their teachers' wives, who go in unto the wombs of beasts, and who follow the law of animals.
t.1.79.15: Druhyu, take upon yourself my old age, which destroys complexion and beauty, for a thousand years, and give me your own youth.
t.1.79.16: But when a thousand years are complete, I will give back your youth, and I will take back again my own evil together with old age.
t.1.79.17: Druhyu said: An old man enjoys neither elephant nor chariot nor horse, nor a woman, and his speech falters; therefore I do not desire old age.
t.1.79.18: Since you, born from my heart, do not give me your own youth, therefore, Druhyu, your cherished desire shall never be fulfilled anywhere.
t.1.79.19: In the land where crossing is always made by rafts and boats, there you, without kingship, together with your lineage, shall obtain the name of Bhoja.
t.1.79.20: O Anu, take upon yourself my sin together with my old age, so that I may live for a single thousand years with your youth.
t.1.79.21: The worn-out old man takes his food at the wrong time like a child, and like one who is impure he does not offer oblations into the fire at the proper time; that old age I do not desire.
t.1.79.24: Pūru, you are my beloved son, and you will be the most excellent. Old age, wrinkles and grey hairs have overtaken me, my dear son, through the curse of Kāvya Uśanas, yet I am not sated with youth.
t.1.79.22: Since you, though born from my very heart, will not give me your own youth, and have spoken of this fault of old age, therefore you yourself shall come to suffer it.
t.1.79.23: Your offspring, O Anu, will perish as soon as they reach youth, and you yourself will likewise become one given to casting out the sacred fires.
t.1.79.25: O Anu, take upon yourself my affliction together with my old age; for some time I would roam among the pleasures of the senses with your youth.
t.1.79.26: But when a full thousand years have passed, I shall give back your youth, and I shall take back my own sin together with old age.
t.1.79.27: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Pūru answered his father at once: "As you have told me, great king, so shall I carry out your word."
t.1.79.28: I shall take upon myself your sin, O king, together with your old age; take my youth from me and enjoy pleasures as you desire.
t.1.79.30: Pūru, I am pleased with you, my child, and being pleased I give you this: your people in your kingdom shall be rich in the fulfilment of all their desires.
t.1.79.29: Covered with old age, bearing your years and your form, I shall give up my youth so that it becomes yours, and I will act just as you tell me.
